perspective:
**Ethan’s available information:**

- Ethan knows he is Gary’s long-time friend from middle school and that Gary is a doctor.
- He directly noticed Gary working excessively long hospital hours, skipping meals, and sacrificing sleep. He became concerned about Gary’s health.
- He invited Gary to a two-day weekend retreat for relaxation. He heard Gary initially decline, saying he appreciated the concern but had too much to do at the hospital.
- At the retreat, Ethan observed Gary acting restless and avoiding discussions about work. Ethan suspected there was more to Gary’s overworking than professional obligations.
- Ethan told Gary they had been friends since middle school, that Gary could tell him anything, and that he was there to help, not judge. Gary replied that it was complicated and he didn’t want to burden Ethan.
- Gary opened up to Ethan about pressures from managing a new department and personal challenges. Ethan felt relief and empathy, then suggested prioritizing tasks and delegating responsibilities. Gary agreed and said he could use help organizing his schedule to make time for himself.
- Over the following months, Ethan regularly checked in with Gary about his progress and challenges. Ethan saw Gary making efforts to change. Gary told him things were better, he was less overwhelmed thanks to Ethan’s help, and he had time for a movie last weekend. Ethan felt hopeful and proud and offered to be available whenever Gary needed to talk.
- After a year, Ethan saw Gary managing a healthier work-life balance on his own. Ethan felt satisfied and happy. He told Gary he was always a call away, knew Gary had it, and encouraged him. Gary thanked Ethan, said he couldn’t have done it without his support, and felt more in control.
